name: Halderworks Instrument
note: The source tools/build.py reads. Colour is a hue seed plus, per token, a lightness and chroma anchor and the contrast floor it must hold. The build clamps chroma into sRGB and re-solves lightness when a floor fails, so a changed accent hue produces a full set rather than an unverified one.

color.note: Every colour is solved to a contrast target, not chosen and then checked. 108 text pairs across both themes, 0 below WCAG AA 4.5:1; 90 non-text pairs (focus ring, chart fills, disabled) held to 3:1, 0 below it; 33 tokens, 0 outside the sRGB gamut. Accent hue 198.

tokens.name: hw-ground
tokens.usage: The page or window background. Every screen starts here.

tokens.name: hw-surface
tokens.usage: Cards, panels and table bodies: one step off the ground.

tokens.name: hw-surface-hover
tokens.usage: The hover fill of a row, a menu item or a quiet button. 1.08:1 off surface in light, 1.04:1 in dark: a step the eye finds and the layout does not.

tokens.name: hw-surface-active
tokens.usage: The pressed fill, and the skeleton fill while content loads. One step past hover.

tokens.name: hw-surface-raised
tokens.usage: Things that float over content and can be dismissed: dialogs, popovers, menus. In light theme this is the same white as surface on purpose - what separates them there is the shadow. In dark theme it is a real lightness step, because a shadow on a dark ground is invisible.

tokens.name: hw-surface-sunken
tokens.usage: Wells that recede: sidebars, code blocks, an input at rest.

tokens.name: hw-border
tokens.usage: The 1px hairline: card and panel edges, table and cell borders, the tab baseline, chart axes and gridlines, the masthead rule, a framed quotation. Separates a container from its ground without being read as an edge.

tokens.name: hw-border-strong
tokens.usage: Control outlines that must be seen: inputs, selects, textareas, checkboxes, switches, slider rails, secondary buttons, the selected segment of a segmented control, and a floating panel's edge. Held to WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 as a control boundary: 3.03:1 at worst in both themes. The first two passes shipped it at 1.64:1 light and 1.92:1 dark on hw-surface.

tokens.name: hw-text
tokens.usage: Primary text. 14.83:1 on ground, 15.78:1 on surface, 13.98:1 on surface-sunken.

tokens.name: hw-text-secondary
tokens.usage: Supporting text, descriptions, metadata. 6.37:1 on ground.

tokens.name: hw-text-muted
tokens.usage: Column heads, placeholders, timestamps. 4.88:1 on ground, the floor of this system.

tokens.name: hw-text-disabled
tokens.usage: Text and icons in a disabled control. Held to the 3:1 non-text bar, not to AA, and solved per theme because one opacity cannot mean one thing in both: hw-text at 45% composites to 1.73:1 in light and 7.40:1 in dark.

tokens.name: hw-ink
tokens.usage: The primary action fill: one filled button per screen, and the selected segment of a segmented control. Carries no hue so the accent stays scarce.

tokens.name: hw-ink-hover
tokens.usage: Hover state of a primary action.

tokens.name: hw-ink-active
tokens.usage: The pressed fill of a primary button. One step past hover in the same direction, so a press is distinguishable from a hover on the one control that commits an action.

tokens.name: hw-ink-text
tokens.usage: Text and icons on an ink fill. 17.63:1 on ink.

tokens.name: hw-accent
tokens.usage: The one brand hue. Links, selected state, live state, focus. 5.09:1 on ground.

tokens.name: hw-accent-hover
tokens.usage: Hover state of an accent link or accent fill.

tokens.name: hw-accent-quiet
tokens.usage: A flat accent tint for a selected row or an accent badge. Solved so hw-accent clears AA on it, which the first pass asserted but never checked.

tokens.name: hw-accent-ring
tokens.usage: The focus ring, at 2px with a 2px offset. Held to the WCAG 2.2 non-text bar of 3:1 against the surface CLOSEST to it in lightness, not against the ground: solved against the ground alone it measured 2.56:1 on hw-surface-raised in dark theme.

tokens.name: hw-success
tokens.usage: Passed, verified, settled: a badge, a validation summary, a positive delta against a baseline. Never a brand colour. 5.10:1 on ground.

tokens.name: hw-success-quiet
tokens.usage: Fill behind success text in a badge or banner. Solved so hw-success clears AA on it, which the first pass asserted but never checked.

tokens.name: hw-warning
tokens.usage: Retried, degraded, expiring: a badge, an inline alert, a banner on a partial load. 5.10:1 on ground. Dark amber rather than yellow because no yellow clears 4.5:1 on a light ground.

tokens.name: hw-warning-quiet
tokens.usage: Fill behind warning text in a badge or banner. Solved so hw-warning clears AA on it, which the first pass asserted but never checked.

tokens.name: hw-danger
tokens.usage: Failed, revoked, destructive: a badge, a field error border, a destructive menu item, a negative delta. 5.09:1 on ground.

tokens.name: hw-danger-quiet
tokens.usage: Fill behind danger text in a badge or banner. Solved so hw-danger clears AA on it, which the first pass asserted but never checked.

tokens.name: hw-chart-1
tokens.usage: First data series. Shares the accent hue so the primary series reads as the subject.

tokens.name: hw-chart-2
tokens.usage: Second data series, in bars, lines, areas and their direct labels. Never a state.

tokens.name: hw-chart-3
tokens.usage: Third data series, in bars, lines, areas and their direct labels. Never a state.

tokens.name: hw-chart-4
tokens.usage: Fourth data series, in bars, lines, areas and their direct labels. Never a state.

tokens.name: hw-chart-5
tokens.usage: Fifth data series, in bars, lines, areas and their direct labels. Never a state.

tokens.name: hw-chart-6
tokens.usage: Sixth data series. Six is the limit; past that, group the tail.

tokens.name: hw-scrim
tokens.usage: Behind a dialog only. Nothing else dims the page.

styles.usage: Long-form running text in docs and release notes. Measure 68ch.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: A run is immutable once it settles.
styles.usage: The default for product UI. Measure 56ch.

styles.name: body-sm
styles.usage: Dense UI: table cells, list rows, control labels, help text.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: A control's own label, a hint, a badge.

styles.name: micro
styles.usage: Column heads and eyebrows, set uppercase. Nothing smaller exists.

spacing.note: Base unit 4px. Ten steps; 2px exists for one case only.

tokens.name: hw-space-2
tokens.usage: The badge's vertical inset, and nothing else. At 4px a micro badge stands taller than the label beside it. The icon-to-label gap is --hw-icon-gap at 6px; this token claimed that job too and did not have it.

tokens.name: hw-space-4
tokens.usage: Inside a badge or a chip; the gap between a label and its control.

tokens.name: hw-space-8
tokens.usage: Between controls in a row; padding inside a dense table cell.

tokens.name: hw-space-12
tokens.usage: Padding inside a button or input; the gap between list rows.

tokens.name: hw-space-16
tokens.usage: Padding inside a card; the gap between cards.

tokens.name: hw-space-24
tokens.usage: Between a heading and its content; padding in a dialog.

tokens.name: hw-space-32
tokens.usage: Padding at a screen's edge; between sections of a form.

tokens.name: hw-space-48
tokens.usage: Between major sections of a page.

tokens.name: hw-space-64
tokens.usage: Above and below a page heading on a marketing surface.

tokens.name: hw-space-96
tokens.usage: Between bands on a marketing surface. The largest step; nothing is bigger.

radius.note: Three sizes and a pill, each bound to a role. One radius everywhere removes the only non-colour cue for what contains what.

tokens.name: hw-radius-sm
tokens.usage: Things inside other things: badges, checkboxes, swatches, the status dot.

tokens.name: hw-radius-md
tokens.usage: Interactive controls: buttons, inputs, selects, menu items, tabs.

tokens.name: hw-radius-lg
tokens.usage: Containers: cards, panels, dialogs, popovers, toasts.

tokens.name: hw-radius-full
tokens.usage: Avatars and count pills only, where the shape itself carries the meaning.

shadow.note: Two shadows. Inside a window they are light-theme only, because a shadow on a dark ground is invisible and dark elevation is carried by surface lightness instead; across 14 measured reference products, 73 of 75 sampled elements carried box-shadow: none. The one exception is a panel floating over content this system does not own, such as a menu-bar panel, which keeps its shadow in BOTH themes because there is no surface lightness under it to carry the step. Dark values have always been present in this file; only the prose forbade them.

tokens.name: hw-shadow-overlay
tokens.usage: Popovers, menus and toasts in light theme. Dark theme carries elevation by surface lightness instead.

tokens.name: hw-shadow-dialog
tokens.usage: Dialogs and sheets in light theme, the only element allowed a shadow this large, and a menu-bar panel in both themes (36-form-factors.md).

duration.note: Four durations. 150ms is the default; 40-motion.md owns what may animate.

tokens.name: hw-duration-instant
tokens.usage: A state change the user is already looking at: a checkbox tick, a switch knob, a segmented-control fill.

tokens.name: hw-duration-fast
tokens.usage: The default for every transition: hover fills, focus rings, border colour, disclosure. 0.15s is the most-used duration across the reference set.

tokens.name: hw-duration-base
tokens.usage: Something entering or leaving the layer stack: a popover, a menu, a toast.

tokens.name: hw-duration-slow
tokens.usage: A dialog or a sheet, where the scrim and the panel move together and the user must follow both.

easing.note: Three curves. Motion answers an action; it does not decorate an arrival.

tokens.name: hw-ease-out
tokens.usage: The default, for anything appearing or responding to a press: fast at the start, settled at the end.

tokens.name: hw-ease-in
tokens.usage: Only for something leaving the screen, where the exit should not compete for attention.

tokens.name: hw-ease-standard
tokens.usage: A value moving between two on-screen positions, such as a slider thumb or a progress fill.

layout.note: The grid, its breakpoints and the widths a page is allowed to be.

tokens.name: hw-bp-sm
tokens.usage: Phone to small tablet. Below it a screen is one column and the rail is a sheet.

tokens.name: hw-bp-md
tokens.usage: The measured consensus edge: 23 of 44 captured sites declare a 768px min-width, more than any other value.

tokens.name: hw-bp-lg
tokens.usage: Second most declared, on 18 of 44. The rail becomes permanent here.

tokens.name: hw-bp-xl
tokens.usage: Declared on 12 of 44. The content column stops growing; the margins take the rest.

tokens.name: hw-bp-2xl
tokens.usage: Only a wide table or a three-pane shell uses the extra width. Prose never does.

tokens.name: hw-gutter-sm
tokens.usage: Page margin below hw-bp-md. Measured at 390px wide: 16px on 6 of 12 sites, 24px on 3.

tokens.name: hw-gutter-md
tokens.usage: Page margin from hw-bp-md to hw-bp-lg.

tokens.name: hw-gutter-lg
tokens.usage: Page margin at hw-bp-lg and above.

tokens.name: hw-column-gap
tokens.usage: The gutter between grid columns. 24px is the fourth most used column-gap in the capture (93 uses) and the largest that stays on the 4px grid at every step.

tokens.name: hw-columns
tokens.usage: Twelve columns above hw-bp-lg, six from hw-bp-md, four below. 58 of the grids sampled use twelve.

tokens.name: hw-container-app
tokens.usage: The app shell's cap. Past it the content pane stops and the window grows around it.

tokens.name: hw-container-page
tokens.usage: Marketing and documentation. The 1100-1300 band is the most occupied in the capture: 20 of 44 sites.

tokens.name: hw-container-prose
tokens.usage: A reading column on its own. The median measured prose column at 1440px across the capture is 721px.

tokens.name: hw-measure-ui
tokens.usage: Running text inside product UI.

tokens.name: hw-measure-prose
tokens.usage: Long-form. The median measured running-text width across 30 sites is 64ch; 68ch sits inside the comfortable band and above the product step.

tokens.name: hw-rail
tokens.usage: The app shell's navigation rail at hw-bp-lg and above.

tokens.name: hw-rail-collapsed
tokens.usage: The rail reduced to icons, which is the only collapsed state it has.

tokens.name: hw-panel-w
tokens.usage: A menu-bar utility panel. 40ch of body-sm Public Sans measures 318.4px with the face loaded, plus hw-cell-pad-x each side, rounded up to the 4px grid.

tokens.name: hw-panel-max-h
tokens.usage: A menu-bar panel's ceiling: a 32px header, 12 rows at hw-row-h-compact and a 48px footer. Always clamped further by min(, calc(100vh - hw-space-48)).

density.note: Two settings. Compact changes vertical rhythm and control height; it never changes type size, colour, alignment or horizontal padding.

tokens.name: hw-control-h-sm
tokens.usage: Compact control height: a toolbar button, an inline filter.

tokens.name: hw-control-h
tokens.usage: The default control height. 32px is the most common measured button height in the capture, on 14 of 44 sites.

tokens.name: hw-control-h-lg
tokens.usage: A single call to action on a marketing surface. Second most measured, on 11 sites.

tokens.name: hw-row-h
tokens.usage: Comfortable table or list row: 13px text on 1.5 leading plus 12px above and below.

tokens.name: hw-row-h-compact
tokens.usage: Compact row. The same text, 6px above and below, and nothing else changes.

tokens.name: hw-cell-pad-x
tokens.usage: Horizontal cell padding, both densities. Density changes the vertical rhythm, never the column alignment.

tokens.name: hw-cell-pad-y
tokens.usage: Vertical cell padding, comfortable.

tokens.name: hw-cell-pad-y-compact
tokens.usage: Vertical padding in a table cell and a list row under data-density="compact". Horizontal padding does not change, which is what keeps a column in the same place across the toggle.

tokens.name: hw-field-pad-x
tokens.usage: Horizontal padding inside a field, a select, a stepper and a search box. Unchanged by density, like hw-cell-pad-x, so a column of controls keeps its left edge across the toggle. Was an unnamed 10px literal in the Input anatomy, off the 4px grid.

tokens.name: hw-field-pad-y
tokens.usage: Input vertical padding, comfortable.

tokens.name: hw-field-pad-y-compact
tokens.usage: Input vertical padding, compact.

icon.note: One 16px grid, one stroke weight, one alignment rule.

tokens.name: hw-icon-sm
tokens.usage: Inside a badge or beside 12px label text.

tokens.name: hw-icon
tokens.usage: The default. 16x16 is the most widely used rendered icon size in the capture: 21 of 44 sites.

tokens.name: hw-icon-lg
tokens.usage: A toolbar or rail icon that carries its own hit target.

tokens.name: hw-icon-stroke
tokens.usage: Stroke weight at 16px and 20px. 1.5px on 8 sites, 2px on 12; 1.5px is the lighter of the two and the one that survives beside 13px text.

tokens.name: hw-icon-gap
tokens.usage: Icon to its own label. Below the 4px grid on purpose: 4px reads as one object, 8px as two.

zIndex.note: Seven layers. A number that is not on this list is a layer nobody decided on.

tokens.name: hw-z-base
tokens.usage: Page content.

tokens.name: hw-z-sticky
tokens.usage: A sticky table head or a pinned toolbar.

tokens.name: hw-z-rail
tokens.usage: The app shell's rail when it overlays content below hw-bp-lg.

tokens.name: hw-z-dropdown
tokens.usage: Menu, select, popover, tooltip.

tokens.name: hw-z-scrim
tokens.usage: The dialog scrim.

tokens.name: hw-z-dialog
tokens.usage: The dialog itself.

tokens.name: hw-z-toast
tokens.usage: Toasts, which must clear a dialog because they report what the dialog did.

stroke.note: Line weights, separated from colour so a border's thickness is one decision.

tokens.name: hw-border-w
tokens.usage: Every border in the system. There is no 2px border.

tokens.name: hw-focus-w
tokens.usage: The focus ring. 2px is the most used real outline-width in the capture: 246 declarations against 75 at 1px.

tokens.name: hw-focus-offset
tokens.usage: The gap between the control's own edge and its ring, so the ring reads as a ring.

tokens.name: hw-tab-active-w
tokens.usage: The rule under the selected tab, which is the one place a 2px line is a state.

grid.note: The unit governs space and size: how far apart two things are, and how big a thing is. It does not govern a radius, which is a curve rather than a distance along an axis, and it does not govern a line weight. It also does not govern the line box, which is a type size times a line-height and lands where readability puts it: 0 of the 10 type steps produce a line box on the unit, and forcing them there would mean choosing leading to satisfy arithmetic. tools/build.py refuses to emit an off-unit value in scope that is not named below, and refuses an entry below whose value has since moved onto the unit.

exceptions.hw-space-2: The badge's vertical inset. At 4px a micro badge stands taller than the label text beside it and the row grows around it.
exceptions.hw-icon-gap: 6px, between an icon and its own label. Derived optically rather than arithmetically: 4px reads as one object and 8px as two.
exceptions.hw-icon-sm: 14px, beside 12px label text. An icon on the unit either matches the cap height at 12px, which is too small to read, or overshoots it at 16px.
exceptions.hw-field-pad-y: Consequence, not choice. --hw-control-h is the token and the padding is what is left after the line box and the border; 65-components.md records the 35.5px field beside a 32px button that this rule was written from.
exceptions.hw-field-pad-y-compact: The same consequence at the compact control height.
exceptions.hw-cell-pad-y-compact: The same consequence at the compact row height: 19.5px of line box plus 6px above and below is the 32px compact row.
exceptions.hw-icon-stroke: A line weight rather than a distance. 55-iconography.md solves it to a constant painted stroke at every rendered size: 1.5px in the house, and 1.75px or 2px in a brand that takes one.

brand.note: What a product's brand seed may choose from. tools/build.py --brand checks every input against its bound, applies it to a copy of this seed, and solves that copy with the same code as the house set, so a brand is a rebuild and never a hand-pick. design/12-brand.md owns the rule; the bounds on the numeric inputs are pinned in tools/build.py rather than here, so an edit to this file cannot widen them.

vivid.note: The vivid tier: tokens a brand seed opts into by naming brandLightness and brandChroma. A brand that names neither emits exactly the house token set. tools/build.py appends these to the brand's copy of the seed and solves them with the rest; a role other than a plain solve is named in `role`. design/12-brand.md#the-vivid-tier owns the rule, and tools/contrast.py declares every pair below on its own.

tokens.name: hw-brand
tokens.usage: The brand's one vivid fill, at the lightness and chroma the brand seed names, clipped to sRGB: a primary button when primary is brand, a highlight, a chip, the active rail row, a progress fill. Its label is hw-on-brand and nothing else.
tokens.notFor: Text, a border, a focus ring, a state, or a fill under data text. It carries no contrast floor of its own; its label carries the floor and moves it if it has to.

tokens.name: hw-brand-hover
tokens.usage: hw-brand under the pointer: 0.03 of lightness toward its label, solved so the label still clears.
tokens.notFor: Anything but the hover of an hw-brand fill.

tokens.name: hw-brand-active
tokens.usage: hw-brand while pressed: 0.06 of lightness toward its label, solved so the label still clears.
tokens.notFor: Anything but the pressed state of an hw-brand fill.

tokens.name: hw-on-brand
tokens.usage: The label on hw-brand and its two states: hw-text or hw-ink-text, whichever clears higher on the fill. When neither clears, the fill moves rather than the label.
tokens.notFor: Any ground but the three hw-brand fills.

tokens.name: hw-brand-quiet
tokens.usage: A quiet tint of the brand hue behind a brand chip, a feature icon's disc or a highlighted phrase in running text. hw-text holds 7:1 on it.
tokens.notFor: A selected row, which is hw-select, or a status block, which is a state's own quiet fill.

tokens.name: hw-field
tokens.usage: A large vivid area: a welcome, an empty state, a hero or a carousel cover. It carries display copy and one action, or stages one of the product's own objects with corner labels and annotations, all in hw-on-field.
tokens.notFor: Data, a table, a list of rows, or hw-text-secondary. A field is never under data.

tokens.name: hw-on-field
tokens.usage: The ink on hw-field: hw-text or hw-ink-text, whichever clears higher.

tokens.name: hw-select
tokens.usage: The selected row's fill. With selection: neutral it is a neutral step past hw-surface-active, and it is exempt from the accent's fill bar because it is not a hue; with selection: accent it is hw-accent-quiet's value. hw-text holds 7:1 on it.
tokens.notFor: A status, a hover or a pressed fill.

tokens.name: hw-primary
tokens.usage: The loudest control's fill: hw-ink's value, or hw-brand's when the brand seed says primary: brand.
tokens.notFor: Anything but the one primary action in a view.

tokens.name: hw-primary-hover
tokens.usage: hw-primary under the pointer: hw-ink-hover or hw-brand-hover, with hw-primary.
tokens.notFor: Anything but the hover of hw-primary.

tokens.name: hw-primary-active
tokens.usage: hw-primary while pressed: hw-ink-active or hw-brand-active, with hw-primary.
tokens.notFor: Anything but the pressed state of hw-primary.

tokens.name: hw-on-primary
tokens.usage: The label on hw-primary: hw-ink-text or hw-on-brand, with hw-primary.
tokens.notFor: Any ground but the three hw-primary fills.
